messages.content: Explain why the leaves of many trees change color in autumn. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: As autumn brings shorter days and cooler temperatures, trees stop producing chlorophyll, the green pigment they use to make food. When the green fades, other pigments that were hidden inside the leaves all summer—like yellow and orange—finally show through. Some trees also produce new red and purple pigments during this transition, creating the bright fall colors we see before the leaves eventually drop.
